data.narrative:
Spaceium is a Seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Ashi Dissanayake (orbital mechanics, NASA aerodynamics background) and Reza Fetanat (mechanical engineering, cryogenics expertise). The company has raised $6.3M to date. The Space & Aerospace sector comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Stage-progression analysis, applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-round advancement, yields $15.75M from the $6.3M raised base. Peer-median anchoring is not applicable; while 14 same-sector peers exist, fewer than 3 datapoints survive filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables. Public-comp P/S anchoring cannot be deployed without disclosed revenue figures, common among private companies. The Space & Aerospace public universe exhibits a median P/S of 27.4x, but remains unusable absent target revenue.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $13M–$18M, with a median estimate of $16M. This range rests on a single applicable method and therefore carries material uncertainty. Key risks include limited peer visibility at the Seed stage in deep-tech aerospace, absence of revenue disclosure, and reliance on stage-step multiples that may not reflect Spaceium's technical differentiation or capital efficiency. Additional data on run rate, customer traction, or IP validation would materially improve conviction.
